memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Abraham said, "I swear it." Then Abraham complained to Abimelek about a well of water that Abimelek's servants had seized. But Abimelek said, "I don't know who has done this. You did not tell me, and I heard about it only today." - Gen 21:24-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abraham enters into a solemn agreement - "I swear it" - and the two men work through a real dispute. There had been a conflict: Abimelech's servants had seized one of Abraham's wells. Rather than letting resentment simmer or the conflict fester, Abraham brings it into the open, and Abimelech responds honestly: "I don't know who has done this... I heard about it only today." Two men committed to their word deal with a problem directly and truthfully.

There is a quiet wisdom here about handling conflict. Abraham didn't nurse a grudge in silence, and he didn't retaliate. He raised the issue plainly. And Abimelech didn't get defensive; he answered honestly. This is how people of integrity handle disputes - directly, truthfully, seeking resolution rather than revenge.

Notice too the emphasis on oaths and truthfulness. In a world where a person's word could be trusted, agreements held weight, and honesty about wrongs cleared the way for peace. Both men valued keeping their word and speaking truth, and it made reconciliation possible.

This reflects God's own heart, for He is a God who always keeps His word and speaks truth. His people are called to be the same - to "let your yes be yes and your no be no" (Matt 5:37), to keep our commitments even when costly (Ps 15:4), and to address conflicts honestly rather than harbouring resentment. Where do you need to bring a simmering issue into the open, or keep a word you've given? Integrity in our dealings honours the God of truth.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you keeping the commitments and promises you've made?
- Is there a conflict you need to address honestly rather than letting it fester?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You always keep Your word and speak truth. Help me be a person of integrity who keeps commitments and handles conflict honestly, seeking peace rather than nursing resentment. Make me trustworthy like You.
Amen.
